---
title: "Reading configuration with `get-config`"
---

`quarto get-config` prints the configuration that applies to a document,
*after* Quarto has merged every source of metadata. Use it when an external
tool needs to know a document's effective settings without re-implementing
Quarto's metadata rules.

```bash
quarto get-config <file> [path]
```

Quarto resolves configuration from several places — the project's
`_quarto.yml`, `_metadata.yml` files in enclosing directories, the document's
own YAML front matter, and format-specific blocks such as `format: html:`.
`get-config` applies all of these in the same order a render would and reports
the result as JSON.

## Selecting a value

With no path, the entire merged configuration is printed:

```bash
quarto get-config report.qmd
```

Pass a dot-separated path to select a single value. A numeric segment indexes
into a list:

```bash
quarto get-config report.qmd title
quarto get-config report.qmd authors.0.name
```

If the path does not exist, `get-config` prints `null` and exits successfully.
Pass `--strict` to make a missing path an error instead.

## Choosing a format

Some settings depend on the output format (for example, `toc` may be enabled
for HTML but not for PDF). By default `get-config` reports the configuration for
HTML. Use `--to` to choose another format:

```bash
quarto get-config report.qmd toc --to html   # e.g. true
quarto get-config report.qmd toc --to pdf    # e.g. false
```

## Text vs. Pandoc output

Front-matter values like `title` may contain Markdown. By default these are
returned as Markdown strings:

```bash
quarto get-config report.qmd title
# "Hello *world*!"
```

Pass `--output pandoc` to get the parsed Pandoc abstract syntax tree instead,
which is useful if your tool already works with Pandoc's JSON:

```bash
quarto get-config report.qmd title --output pandoc
# [{"t":"Str","c":"Hello"},{"t":"Space"},
#  {"t":"Emph","c":[{"t":"Str","c":"world"}]},{"t":"Str","c":"!"}]
```

## Options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--to <format>` | Format whose settings are merged in (default: `html`). |
| `--output <value\|pandoc>` | How Markdown values are rendered (default: `value`). |
| `--strict` | Exit with an error if the requested path does not exist. |
| `--compact` | Print single-line JSON instead of pretty-printed output. |

## Piping to other tools

The output is plain JSON, so it composes with tools like
[`jq`](https://jqlang.github.io/jq/):

```bash
quarto get-config report.qmd --compact | jq '.authors[].name'
```
